Posterior probability that a diagnostic exceeds a value

Source: R/accessors.R
prob_above.Rd

Computes the posterior probability that the informativeness, the mean reliability, the concentration count or the between-site standard deviation is above a given value.

Usage

prob_above(x, threshold = NULL, which = c("I", "mean", "J_eff", "sigma_tau"))

Arguments

x

An object of class reliability_posterior or reliability_draws.

threshold

The value, a single number. For which = "I", NULL (the default) uses the threshold of the fit; for the other quantities a value must be given.

which

The quantity: one of "I" (the default), "mean", "J_eff" or "sigma_tau".

Value

A number between 0 and 1. For draws, its attribute mcse is the Monte Carlo standard error.

Details

The four quantities increase with sigma_tau, so the probability is \(1 - F(\sigma_c)\), where \(F\) is the posterior distribution function of sigma_tau and \(\sigma_c\) the value at which the quantity equals the threshold. For the informativeness and a threshold \(c\), \(\sigma_c = \{\mathrm{GM}(v)\, c/(1-c)\}^{1/2}\). When all sampling variances are equal, the concentration count is the constant \(J\); its probability of strictly exceeding \(c\) is 1 for \(c < J\) and 0 for \(c \ge J\).

Lee (2026) reports the probability that \(I\) exceeds 1/2, the value at which the between-site variance equals the geometric mean of the sampling variances. Above it the leading term of the mean reliability minus \(I\) is negative (Proposition 2), although the remainder can change the sign of the difference. The value 1/2 is a reference point, not a standard that an analysis must meet.

References

Lee, J. (2026). The geometry of informativeness: A Bregman-centroid diagnostic for partial pooling in multisite trials. Unpublished manuscript.

See also

plot_functionals(), whose label gives this probability.

Examples

fit <- reliability_posterior(estimate, se = se, data = eight_schools)
prob_above(fit)
#> [1] 0.1379141
prob_above(fit, threshold = 0.3)
#> [1] 0.3122938
prob_above(fit, threshold = 5, which = "sigma_tau")
#> [1] 0.5194775
